svg.title: Density of freshwater
svg.desc: Density of freshwater in g/cm³ versus temperature from 0 to 12 °C. The density rises from 0.99984 g/cm³ at 0 °C to a maximum of 0.99997 g/cm³ at 4 °C, then falls ever more steeply, to 0.99950 g/cm³ at 12 °C. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Why lakes freeze from the top down
Colder surface water is denser: it sinks, mixing the lake
Below 4 °C the surface is lighter: it stays on top
Ice forms on top; the deep water stays at 4 °C
Quadratic fit to freshwater density between 0 and 12 °C (±0.00005 g/cm³). The density change is tiny,
but enough to drive or stop convection.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
